title: oauth: on a private plain-HTTP deployment the authorization-server metadata publishes an `https://` issuer while `authorization_servers[0]` and every endpoint are `http://` (RFC 8414 §3.3 mismatch)
body:
On a deployment that serves OAuth over plain HTTP on a private host, the authorization-server metadata publishes an `https://` issuer. Every other OAuth URL on that boot is `http://`: the protected-resource document's `authorization_servers` entry and every endpoint in the metadata. RFC 8414 §3.3 requires the metadata's `issuer` to be identical to the authorization-server URL the client was given. A client that validates it will refuse the discovery, so the private-host OAuth track the deployment advertises may not complete end to end.

QA-source: #26468 · ai.mcp-oauth-private-host-transport · observed beside the clauses

## Reproduction (framework 756220c4, stock showcase)

1. Boot with a private-host base URL:
   `OS_PORT=41566 OS_AUTH_URL=http://10.20.30.40:41566 pnpm -C examples/app-showcase exec objectstack dev --ui --seed-admin --no-compile --no-watch -p 41566 -d file:/tmp/x/data.db`
   The boot log warns, as designed: `OAuth is served UNENCRYPTED … (http://10.20.30.40:41566/api/v1/auth) … accepts this origin only because the host is loopback or a private / link-local address`.
2. `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` returns `resource: http://10.20.30.40:41566/api/v1/mcp` and `authorization_servers: ['http://10.20.30.40:41566/api/v1/auth']`.
3. `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/api/v1/auth` returns:
   - `issuer: https://10.20.30.40:41566/api/v1/auth` (scheme `https`);
   - `token_endpoint: http://10.20.30.40:41566/api/v1/auth/oauth2/token` (scheme `http`).
4. `GET /api/v1/auth/.well-known/openid-configuration` returns the same `https` issuer with `http` endpoints.

- **Expected:** `issuer` = `http://10.20.30.40:41566/api/v1/auth`, the value in `authorization_servers[0]` and in the boot's own warning line.
- **Actual:** the scheme is rewritten to `https`.

The QA runner reproduced it on two fresh boots, and it was reproduced again on an independent verification boot. A public-origin boot shows the same shape (its discovery is refused anyway), and a loopback origin is consistent.

## Mechanism (from the runner's trace, to confirm)

`validateIssuerUrl()` in `@better-auth/oauth-provider` 1.7.12 rewrites a non-loopback `http` issuer to `https`. ObjectStack's transport rule accepts private and link-local plain-HTTP origins, so the two disagree on exactly the origins the platform admits.

## Notes

- This fails closed. It is an interoperability defect, not an authorization hole: no token or code is issued to the wrong party.
- No ledger clause asserts that the metadata `issuer` equals `authorization_servers[0]`. That gap is parked on the wave anchor #25807 as a checklist-accuracy finding.
- Full evidence chain: the run record named in the QA-source line above.
